All three calls completed and returned usable data.

## What came back

**(1) `category='ai'`** — 92 tools, every entry with a `name` and `description`.

**(2) `query='search'`** — 11 tools, every entry with a `name` and `description`.

**(3) `toolName='generate_image'`** — full detail: name, description, complete `parameters` schema (`prompt` required; optional `model` enum with 44 ids; optional `inputMediaUrl`), plus example input and response.

## What's off

- **Raw internal API routes are exposed as tool names.** The `ai` category contains entries like `vibe_agent_chat_threads_threadId_messages_messageId_vote_POST` and `vibe_agent_chat_folders_subfolders_subFolderId_permissions_GET` — HTTP verbs and camelCase path parameters baked straight into names the user sees, sitting right next to clean ones like `rename-thread`.

- **`tool-help` contradicts its own description.** It advertises "Default page size for AI/MCP is 25" and pagination via `page`/`pageSize`, but `category='ai'` returned all 92 tools in one unpaginated response.

- **`generate_image` points at a tool name that doesn't exist.** Its description says "Use list-models with modelType=image" — the tool is `models`; `list-models` is only an alias. The same wrong name is repeated in the `model` parameter description.

- **`generate_image.inputMediaUrl` uses video wording.** "The model animates or transforms from this image" — "animates" was copied over from the video tool.

- **Inconsistent entry shapes.** Several entries (`describe_image`, `describe_video`, `generate_image`, `generate_music`, `generate_video`, `models`) have no `title`, while their neighbours do. Call 2's entries carry a `category` field that call 1's entries lack.

None of these blocked the calls — all three returned correct, complete data — but the raw route names shouldn't be reaching a user at all.
